title: Classic Reuben with Corned Beef, Sauerkraut and Russian-Style Dressing
summary: Hot pressed sandwiches layered with warm corned beef, tangy sauerkraut and melted cheese between slices of rye, finished with a creamy dressing.
equipment: 30 cm heavy frying pan with a slightly smaller lid

steps.title: Dressing
steps.text: Stir together 35 ml mayonnaise, 30 ml soured cream, 20 ml ketchup, 1 tbsp chopped pickle, 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tsp horseradish, then season with pepper.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Oven 180°C, wrap the 450 g corned beef with 2 tbsp water in foil and heat for 10 min.

steps.title: Sauerkraut
steps.text: Melt 15 g butter in a small pan and cook the sauerkraut until the liquid evaporates and it turns glossy, about 5 min.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Melt 30 g butter in the large pan and toast 4 bread slices on one side until golden, about 4 min.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Spread dressing on all 8 slices, pile the drained beef, sauerkraut and cheese onto the toasted slices, then close with the untoasted slices.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Melt the remaining 25 g butter, add the sandwiches and press with a smaller lid until the cheese melts, about 2 min, then uncover and keep pressing until crisp, about 3 min.

tips: Warm the beef gently in a sealed foil parcel so it stays moist rather than drying out.
Cook off the extra liquid from the sauerkraut so the sandwich doesn't turn soggy.
Press firmly while grilling and move the sandwiches around the pan for even, crisp colouring.
storage: Best eaten hot and freshly made; reheat any leftover beef until piping hot (74°C) before rebuilding the sandwich. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
